title: Natural open-sections cohomology comparison normalized on ordinary complexes
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, U any open of Spec A, with chosen derived categories [def-pc-derived-category]. T is over-restriction followed by the over-equivalence. F is H^0 of derived global sections on U, using the standard derived category of modules over Gamma(U,O_U), with scalars forgotten. G is H^0 of derived affineOpenSections [def-sc-principal-open-alternating-total] with A-scalars forgotten. For an ordinary ambient complex K, alpha_K is the inverse ordinary sections/homology comparison followed by the ordinary-to-derived global-sections unit on T(K) and inverse exact restriction factorization. beta_K is homologyFunctorFactors inverse followed by the ambient ordinary-to-derived sections unit. There is a natural isomorphism e:T.mapDerivedCategory composed with F isomorphic to G with alpha_K followed by e at Q(K) equal to beta_K for every K. No structure class or Hom-set evaluation is asserted.

proof.text: The top open in the over-site corresponds to U. The presheaf image of this equality identifies restricted global sections with ambient open sections. Presheaf naturality proves naturality. Exact scalar forgetting commutes with homology by ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso. These comparisons are implemented without holes.

Extension by zero is an exact left adjoint of over-restriction. The exact-adjoint K-injective criterion shows that over-restriction preserves K-injectives. The over-equivalence also preserves K-injectives, so their composite T does.

For a K-injective J both ordinary-to-derived units are isomorphisms. Conjugate the ordinary cohomology comparison by these units and the exact restriction factorization. Naturality for homotopy maps and full faithfulness of localization on K-injectives descend this to a natural isomorphism on the chosen derived category. For any K, take a quasi-isomorphism K to J. Naturality of the two units proves the square after mapping to J; cancel the derived isomorphism to get the square on K. No quasi-coherence or boundedness is needed.
